title: docs(page): every taught page node names the pageType that draws its heading; schema-reference teaches the five PageType members (objectui#11436)
body:
Fixes #11436

Clause-②: no

## What changed

A `page` node with no `pageType` is a `record` page. `PageRenderer` leaves a record page's `h1` to a `page:header` block and never draws its `description`. So every producer below drew no heading. Each now names the page type that draws what it shows. None of them teaches a detail page, so none moved its heading into a `page:header` block.

| Producer | Fence | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| catalog `simple-page.json` (Page reference, Basic Usage) | file | `app` | The minimal general page. It matches the layout guide's Basic Usage after objectui#11423. |
| catalog `page-with-header.json` (With Title and Description) | file | `app` | A general overview page with a stats grid. |
| catalog `full-dashboard.json` (Dashboard Page) | file | `home` | A KPI landing page. The renderer's own comment calls `home` dashboard-style, with a wider layout. |
| catalog `settings-layout.json` (Settings Page) | file | `utility` | A settings page. The layout guide's Content Width teaches `utility` for settings and forms. |
| catalog `documentation-page.json` (Content Page) | file | `app` | A content page inside an app. |
| `examples/hello-world/schema.json` | file | `app` | The smallest app page. |
| `utilities/runner.mdx` › 1. Plugin Development | `json` | `app` | The runner's index page. |
| `utilities/runner.mdx` › Add Custom Schemas | `jsonc` | `app` | A routed page. |
| `api/schema-reference.md` › Schema Composition | `json` | `app` | A composed CRM page. |
| `guide/schema-playground.md` › Composing Schemas | `json` | `app` | A composed project page. |
| `guide/schema-rendering.md` › Nested Schemas | `json` | `app` | A nested composition. |
| `guide/schema-rendering.md` › The SchemaRenderer Component | `tsx` | `app` | The guide's first `PageNodeSchema`. |
| `guide/schema-rendering.md` › TypeScript Support | `tsx` | `app` | A typed page. |
| `core/schema-renderer.mdx` › Simple Rendering | `tsx` | `app` | The same shape. |
| `components/feedback/toaster.mdx` › In App Layout | `plaintext` | `app` | The page beside a root toaster. |
| `api/schema-reference.md` › PageNodeSchema (Part B) | `json` | `app`, was the refused `detail` | Its title and description are a dashboard's, and `app` draws both. |

`components/layout/page.mdx` gains a paragraph on what `pageType` decides. Its Schema block now declares `pageType` with the five members, and it notes that a record page draws neither `title` nor `description`.

The seat's scan read `json` fences and `.json` files and found ten of these producers. Five more sat outside that scan: the `jsonc` fence in runner.mdx, the three `tsx` fences and the `plaintext` fence in toaster.mdx. They are the same family, so this PR corrects them too, as the dispatch allowed.

## Part B

The PageNodeSchema example in `schema-reference.md` named `"pageType": "detail"`. Its table listed list, detail, form, dashboard, report and custom. I measured the section's own example document on both faces (`safeValidateSchema` and `StrictAnyComponentSchema`), once per value:

- detail, form, dashboard, report and custom are each refused with `invalid_value` at `pageType`.
- list, record, home, app and utility pass.

The card named three of those refusals; all five are refused. The example now names `app`. The `title` and `pageType` rows say what draws, and a `description` row is new. A new "Page types" table lists record, home, app, utility and list, with each kind and what it draws. It points to the layout guide for widths rather than restating them.

## Measured first

These were one-time render probes through the real `SchemaRenderer`, at BASE `52c95a166`. The probe file was not committed.

- Each of the 15 record-page producers, as written, rendered with `data-page-type="record"`, no `h1` and no description.
- The same document with `app`, `home`, `utility` or `list` drew the `h1` and the description. With `record` it drew neither.

## The pin

New file: `packages/components/src/__tests__/page-node-headings-drawn-11436.test.tsx`.

The population is computed. The reader walks every fence of every `.md` / `.mdx` page under `content/docs`, in any language, and every non-test source under `examples`. It parses each one with the TypeScript parser and evaluates its literals. Every object literal whose `type` is `page` is a page node. A node joins the population when it has a `title`, a `description`, or a titled `page:header` block in its children or regions. A navigation entry that targets a page (`type: "page"` with a `pageName`) has none of these, so it stays out. At this head the population is 24 heading nodes, 7 of which also have a description.

What it asserts:

1. Static checks:
   - A node that writes `title` or `description` names a drawing `pageType`. That means every member of the spec's `PageTypeSchema` except `record`, read from `@objectstack/spec/ui`.
   - Any `pageType` it names is a member of that schema.
2. Render: each heading node draws exactly one `h1` with its heading. The `h1` sits inside the `page:header` block when that block owns the heading, and outside any header otherwise. Each node with a description draws it.
3. Live controls:
   - Every node whose heading the page draws, with its `pageType` removed, renders as `record` with no `h1` and no description.
   - The record page whose heading is a `page:header` block (the layout guide's Detail Page with Actions), with that heading moved back onto the page node, draws no `h1`.
4. Floor: the 20 corrected producers, named by file and heading, must still be in the population. That covers this card's 16 and objectui#11423's four. A LIT control requires the population to include a `json`, a `jsonc`, a `tsx` and a `plaintext` fence.
5. Declared shape: a TypeScript interface in a fence that declares a `type: 'page'` node with `title` also declares `pageType`. Today that interface is the one in `page.mdx`.

**It is a sibling that subsumes objectui#11423's pin, and this PR deletes that file.** That pin read only the layout guide's `json` fences, and only lines that open exactly with the `json` fence. Every node it read is in this population. Its four named passages are in the floor, and its two live controls are the general ones in (3). Keeping both would leave two readers, with different fence parsers, asserting one rule over overlapping populations. A change to the mechanism would then have to be re-derived twice. I did not extend it in place because its name and ledger row say "layout guide", and nothing of it would survive. The ledger row in `scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs` moves to the new file, with reads `content/docs/**` and a `markdown-tree` walker. `node scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs --audit` says all candidates are adjudicated.

The catalog's reader tests (`layout-props-conversion.test.tsx`, `grid-columns-key.test.tsx`) find `grid` and `container` nodes inside the demos. Adding `pageType` to the page root moves none of those nodes, so neither file changed. Both ran green below. Nothing reads `examples/hello-world/schema.json` except its `App.tsx`, and the package has no tests: it is the zero-test member that `zero-test-member-exclusion-9106.test.ts` names.

## Reverse verification

Every leg ran from the committed head `727873f0d`, and I wrote down each prediction before its run. Mutations went through objectstack's `ablation-replace.mjs`, whose anchors must hit, or through a script with a trap and absolute paths. Each restore was proven by blob == HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`.

- (a) All 13 producer files restored to BASE, pin unchanged. Predicted red, 39 failed / 21 passed. Got **39 failed / 21 passed**. The failures:
  - both static checks and the declared-shape check;
  - 15 renders;
  - 5 descriptions (the five catalog demos);
  - 16 live controls: 15 nodes with no `pageType`, plus `detail`, which is not a drawing member.
- (b) Deleted the `"pageType": "home"` line in `full-dashboard.json` (anchor 1 → 0). Predicted 4 failed. Got **4 failed / 56 passed**: the record check, plus that node's render, description and live control.
- (c) Put `"detail"` back in schema-reference's PageNodeSchema example. Predicted 2 failed. Got **2 failed / 58 passed**: the member check and that node's live control. `detail` still draws, so its render passes. The member check is the static read that catches it.
- Ledger control: with the new row deleted, `node scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs --audit` exits 1 and names the pin (`unadjudicated-test`).

## Tests and gates (head `727873f0d`)

- The pin: 60 passed. It runs in the `dom` project.
- Package readers of the seven edited docs, `container-max-width-false.test.tsx`, and all of `examples/schema-catalog/` (39 files): Test Files 49 passed (49), Tests 2691 passed (2691).
- Script readers of the edited docs and every importer of `scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs`, including its own `markdown-test-inputs.test.ts`: Test Files 21 passed (21), Tests 966 passed (966).
- `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/components^...' --concurrency=2`: 7 successful. `pnpm --filter @object-ui/components type-check` exits 0, and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly` includes the pin.
- `pnpm check:doc-snippets`, after building its own `--build-filter` closure (35 successful): 775 of 775 blocks judged, 0 failed. None of the edited pages is ungated. `pnpm check:doc-examples` exits 0.
- These all exit 0:
  - `python3 scripts/regenerate-catalog-index.py --check`
  - `check:doc-types`, `check:doc-fences`, `check:doc-example-ids` and `check:doc-example-readers`
  - `node scripts/check-doc-links.mjs`: links valid across 17 scan roots
  - `node scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs --audit`
  - `check:control-bytes` and `check:test-path-roots`
  - `check:new-line-citations`: 0 new citations
  - `check-changeset-presence` (the empty-frontmatter changeset), `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-fixed` and `check-changeset-overwrite`
  - `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check-type-check-coverage` and `check-lint-coverage`
- `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the 17 paths: an ordinary pull request.
- eslint `--no-inline-config --format json` over the 2 changed lintable files: 2 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings. The narrowing holds:
  - `--print-config` gives 119 rules for the pin and 0 for `scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs`.
  - JSON and markdown files have no eslint config.
  - `eslint.config.js` sets no `parserOptions` or `projectService`, and no rule under `eslint-rules/` reads the filesystem (both greps exit 1, against a control grep that hits). So the verdicts on untouched files cannot move.

NOT MEASURED, a declared narrowing:
- The whole `packages/components` suite. This diff adds one test file to that package, deletes one, and changes no source in it. CI runs the full suite.
- The repo-wide `pnpm lint`. CI owns that run.

## Acceptance notes

Found while measuring and left for the seat:

- **The same family, outside the population triage set** (`content/docs/**` and `examples/**`):
  - `objectui generate page NAME` (`generatePage` in `packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts`) writes a page with `title` and no `pageType`, so the generated title never draws. That is released `@object-ui/cli` source, so it needs a changeset and the CLI's unit layer.
  - Two published READMEs teach the same shape: `packages/core/README.md` (a `PageNodeSchema` literal with `title`) and `packages/runner/README.md` (its Example Schema `json` fence).
  - Not filed: `packages/runner/src/App.tsx`'s own fallback page has the shape too. That code path also sets an error, and the error branch renders instead, so the fallback page never draws.
  - The pin's reader would cover the READMEs with one more root. That widens the population triage ruled on, so it is the seat's call.
- **A different defect in an example this PR touches.** `examples/hello-world/schema.json` writes its button's text as `content`. `ButtonSchema` declares `label`, and the renderer reads `label` or children. Measured through the real `SchemaRenderer`, the button draws empty text, and a `label` control draws "Get Started". `safeValidateSchema` accepts the document. `StrictAnyComponentSchema` refuses it with `unrecognized_keys` at the button. It is a different defect class from this card, so it is not fixed here.
- Observation, not filed: `PageRenderer` draws `title` and `description` for a `pageType` outside the spec's enum (in the probe, `detail` drew both). Validation already refuses such a value, so a renderer-side change would only be consumer tolerance. Carrier: none.

Concurrency: `main` gained objectui#11447 after BASE. It touches none of these files. The one docs page it edits, `plugin-charts.mdx`, has no page node, checked on the new tip.
